summary: Sheldon navigates social challenges and his mother’s protective support as he begins high school, showcasing his intellect, humor, and apprehension in a bustling new environment.

video_highlights.highlight: A car drives along a rural road as Sheldon sits in the backseat, reflecting on his disinterest in a driving game.
Sheldon proposes a math-based game, but his mother suggests they simply talk instead.
The mother humorously prays for Sheldon’s well-being, blending humor with her protective instincts.
Outside a school, Sheldon and his mother observe the surroundings, preparing for his first day of high school.
Mary advises Sheldon to remove his bow tie, offering a trip to Radio Shack as a compromise.
Missy reinforces Mary’s advice on handling bullies, adding practical tips for Sheldon.

suggested_clips.description: Sheldon expresses disinterest in a driving game, saying, 'Not really. I always lose,' showcasing his reflective and thoughtful nature.
Sheldon's mother humorously prays, 'Lord, look after my son. Don't let him get stuffed in a gym bag,' blending humor with her protective instincts.
Mary advises Sheldon to remove his bow tie to avoid standing out, highlighting her concern for his social adjustment.
Mary advises Sheldon to deter bullies by saying, 'My dad's a football coach,' emphasizing her practical support for his social challenges.
Sheldon humorously responds to his mother’s offer to accompany him, saying, 'No, although I could have used you in the restroom,' showcasing his wit.
Sheldon remarks, 'It's probably the ammonia. Probably. Okay, let the learning begin,' blending humor with his readiness to start high school.
